messages:
ellie.srv: FYI: ACME (customer) opened an escalation — p99 spikes on embeddings API for dedicated-usw2 since last driver/firmware push. They see 300ms -> 4-12s intermittently.
ellie.srv: Repro steps + curl attached, says spike starts ~10m after instance warmup.
maria-eng: thanks, can you paste the curl and the exact model + route they hit?
ellie.srv: here: ```curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \\ -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \\ -d '{"model":"open-embed-512","input":["hello","world"]}'``` They hit route: /v1/embeddings (model pinned to open-embed-512, batching=auto).

sanju-support: Customer reported no schema/billing changes. They noticed it after our 02:10 UTC maintenance window (driver 530.x + nvme-fw 2.1.7) rolled to their Dedicated pool.

devin-sre: Oof. Initial suspicion: storage IO tail / burst eviction causing kvcache thrash. Can we get iostat/dstat around the spike and dmesg from node?
ellie.srv: Uploaded a short log snippet to the thread. Key lines: ```[02:18:12] api-handler: request latency 4623ms (p99)
[02:18:12] nvme: qdepth spike -> 64 -> 512 in 200ms
[02:18:12] kvcache: evict set 9 (prefetch=false)
[02:18:13] auth: retry count 3 for token refresh, downstream timeout
```
maria-eng: interesting — auth retries show up when downstream storage stalls. Could be host kernel IO scheduling interacting badly with new driver. Any CUDA logs?
devin-sre: I also see these in node metrics: CPU softirq jump, io-wait up, nvme lat p99 crossing 1s. Possible pacing/backpressure from kernel -> GPU nvme path.

ellie.srv: Repro on a small local replica: after warmup, run the curl in a tight loop (100 qps) and I see p95 jump at ~6m mark. Here's the minimal repro (ran in a pod): ```for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -X POST ... & done; sleep 1; done```
sanju-support: Customer requests immediate mitigation — they have production SLOs. Options? rollback? node-level QoS?
maria-eng: Short-term mitigations: 1) move customer to alternate Dedicated pool in eu-west or us-east (fastest), 2) apply kernel IO qdisc tweak (reduce max qdepth / add cfq limiter) on affected hosts, 3) pin to a model variant with smaller IO footprint (embedding quantized). Suggest we offer (1) immediately and (2) cluster-side change as 2-3h window.
devin-sre: Agree. Also we should add an automated fallback: if nvme p99 > 800ms for 2min, route that customer's requests to warm fallback host with known-good firmware. I can prototype route rule.
ellie.srv: I'll offer the customer a hot-move to us-east and enable temporary request-sampling for us to capture full traces.
sanju-support: Please confirm the rollback path if hot-move doesn't help. What is the config to revert driver/firmware?
maria-eng: Ops playbook: firmware rollback requires maintenance and host reboot — not ideal for immediate. Kernel/qdisc tweak is our fastest surgical change (no reboot). Devin, can you make a safe qdisc patch?
devin-sre: On it. Plan: reduce /sys/block/nvme*/queue/nr_requests to 128 and add blk-iopoll timeout adjustments, plus tune cfq fairness: ```for d in /sys/block/nvme*; do echo 128 > $d/queue/nr_requests; done``` Will stage to 3 canary hosts then roll if metrics look stable.
ellie.srv: Customer accepted hot-move while canary roll runs. I've filed INC-20445 and told them ETA ~2h.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Started canary job dd-io-qdisc-patch on hosts: node-482, node-491, node-494 (job id: jb-8842).
devin-sre: Canary metrics after 22m: nvme p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 180ms on node-482, kvcache evict rate halved, API p99 decreased from ~4.5s->450ms for sampled traces. Rolling to rest of pool.
maria-eng: Great. Action items: - ellie: confirm customer telemetry and finalize incident note. - devin: roll qdisc across pool and add routing rule for automatic fallback based on nvme p99 threshold. - sanju: update customer with mitigation summary and credits option if they want.
sanju-support: Noted, sending update now. Thanks team :thumbsup:
ellie.srv: Saving logs/traces in /incidents/INC-20445/archive and will add postmortem once we finish root-cause (suspect host kernel driver+nvme qdepth interaction).
maria-eng: Once rollback path is matured, we should add a runbook entry under eng-infra for "nvme qdepth-induced API p99" with mitigations and monitoring playbooks.
ellie.srv: Closing the support escalation ticket after customer confirms stabilization in 2h.
